items: How does Pebl ensure compliance with local labor laws in 185+ countries? Every country has its own labor laws concerning employment contracts, statutory benefits, taxes, termination, and other matters. These mandates are highly dynamic, requiring continuous oversight to stay ahead of evolving labor law changes. Pebl ensures compliance with local labor laws through a proactive, multi-layered approach. Our regional legal teams monitor regulatory shifts, flag issues before they become problems, and keep every EOR engagement up to date. In addition to our own employment law monitoring, we’re backed by Baker McKenzie, the #1 global employment law firm. Our legal expertise is a big reason why our platform is rated #1 for compliance on G2.

How does Pebl prevent worker misclassification when hiring internationally? It doesn't matter if misclassification is an accidental administrative mistake or an intentional staffing workaround. In most countries, it can trigger audits, retroactive taxes, and fines that can be quite costly. With Pebl as the legal Employer of Record (EOR), your hire is properly classified under local law from day one. You maintain the day-to-day working relationship; we bear the legal responsibility for ensuring appropriate classification, among other mandates.

Does Pebl manage payroll taxes, benefits, employment contracts, onboarding, and offboarding compliance in each country? Yes! Pebl's global EOR services cover the full employment lifecycle, including locally compliant contracts, payroll, tax filings, statutory benefits, paid leave, onboarding, and offboarding processes that align with local labor law requirements. Every component of the complete employment dynamic is connected because we know that a mistake in one area tends to create ripple effects in others. With our AI-powered infrastructure and self-service portal, you can onboard in as little as 24 hours.

What is included in Pebl's EOR pricing? How does it vary by country? Across all markets, Pebl's pricing structure uses a flat-rate model with a single predictable monthly fee per employee. That fee covers EOR services, in-country compliance, payroll, onboarding, expense and leave management, and 24/7 support. For current pricing, reach out to us directly for a custom quote.

How does Pebl's EOR pricing compare to setting up a local entity? Setting up a legal entity in a new country can be incredibly expensive, slow, and operationally heavy. The cost alone can range from five to six figures, depending on the market. The registration process can take several months, and the ongoing expenses can include legal, accounting, and administrative overhead. Not only is our pricing structure significantly lower than the cost of setting up a local entity, but our EOR services let you onboard in as little as 24 hours. You trade high, uncertain costs for speed and a simple, predictable per-employee monthly fee. For companies testing a new market or hiring a small team abroad, the math makes choosing an EOR a no-brainer.

Are there any hidden fees in Pebl's EOR services? No. Pebl provides full transparency with pricing. Before you hire, we share the full employment costs beyond EOR costs, including employer tax contributions and statutory requirements specific to the market you’re hiring in. What you see on the platform is what you pay. Every country carries its own mandatory obligations, and those costs vary. You can rest assured that we don’t mark them up or layer on hidden fees. We strongly believe in providing full visibility before you commit.

How do Pebl's EOR services reduce legal and financial risk when expanding globally? Global hiring risks often stay invisible until you face an audit or a labor dispute. By then, the costs can be high. Pebl owns the legal employer responsibility, so liability for global compliance rests with us rather than with your organization. You keep full control over the work and the relationship. Pebl holds the legal exposure across 185+ countries, backed by in-country experts who stay ahead of regulatory changes before they become your problem.
